description.en: The aim of the experiment is to verify Thevenin’s Theorem.
The Instructions provide step-by-step guidance on how to perform the simulation.
The AI guide will assist you in performing the simulation accurately at each step.
The AUTO CONNECT button makes all the connections automatically.
The CHECK button verifies all the connections to ensure that they are correct.
The ADD button adds the readings to the observation table.

The CALCULATE button auto-fills the resistance and source values in the Calculation Panel. For verification, you have to manually calculate the load current using the Thevenin theorem concept and verify it using the VERIFY button.
The RESET button refresh the simulation to its initial state for a fresh start.
The PRINT button allows you to print the simulation.

The RL slider remains disabled until VTH is recorded. It then starts at 0 Ω. Record the first load-power reading and move the slider one division at a time.

**RL divisions:** 0, 100, 200, 300, 400, 450, 550, 700, 850 and 1000 Ω.

This voltmeter is used to measure the Thevenin equivalent voltage (VTH) across the load terminals with the load resistance disconnected. The measured VTH will be used later to calculate the load current.

**Rating:** 0 - 50 V

This ammeter is used to measure the load current (IL​) flowing through the load resistance (RL​). The measured load current is used to verify Thevenin's Theorem by comparing it with the theoretically calculated current.

**Rating:** 0 - 5 mA

The digital multimeter is used in resistance (Ω) mode to measure the Thevenin equivalent resistance (RTH​) across the load terminals after removing the load resistance and deactivating the independent voltage source (by replacing it with a short circuit), the equivalent resistance across the load terminals is measured.

This section provides the required DC voltage to the circuit. The display shows the active voltage supplied to the circuit, and the slider can be used to set the desired voltage value.

**Rating:** 15 V DC
This section displays the circuit and allows users to make the required connections by dragging and dropping wires between the connection terminals.
The first section records the measured Thevenin resistance (RTH​) and voltage (VTH). The second records load resistance (RL), load current (IL), and load power (PL = IL² × RL).
This section displays the equations used to determine the Thevenin resistance (RTH​), Thevenin voltage (VTH) and Load current (IL).

This is the theoretical verification panel where the Thevenin Theorem will be verified. Enter the required values and compare the calculated load current with the measured load current to verify the theorem.

The Report button generates a summarised report of the simulation. After completing the observation table and theoretical calculations, generate the report. The report will include the time taken to complete the simulation, the apparatus used, recorded readings, the user-calculated result and the conclusion.
